name: Ансамбль из 50 чекпойнтов: неопределённость, выбор и усреднение по геометрии представлений
essence: FlyVis ships an ensemble of 50 connectome-constrained networks (flow/0000/000-049), not a single model. Each one is a different local optimum of the same optic-flow task on the same connectome. The members differ only in their free biophysical parameters: time constants, resting potentials and synapse-strength scales. So far the project has used only model 000. The direction has three cheap uses. (1) Replication: are the fly's re-ID effects a property of FlyVis or only of checkpoint 000? These are +0.14 AP over geometry, +0.044 AP for intact vs rewired connectome, and +0.006 AP over the fly's own 721-facet input. (2) Ensemble as uncertainty: disagreement between K models on the same fovea input can act as a per-track reliability signal (q_match-style), and averaging K signatures gives a standard deep-ensemble feature. (3) Selection or averaging by representational geometry: pick or average models by the CKA/RSA similarity of their responses (the cluster medoid) instead of by task error. FlyVis parameters are tied to named cell types, so there is no permutation symmetry. That makes direct parameter averaging within a response cluster possible.
sources: Lappalainen et al., 'Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system', Nature 2024, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07939-3 (50-model ensemble, UMAP + clustering of responses, 4 clusters, medians over the top-20% models); code https://github.com/TuragaLab/flyvis (Ensemble / EnsembleView API). Karaneen, Schomburg, Chklovskii, 'Reproducibility and model-selection stability in connectome-constrained circuit modeling', bioRxiv, posted 20 Apr 2026, https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.18.717873 (they retrained two new 50-model ensembles; fork https://github.com/eschombu/flyvis/tree/matters-arising). Zhou & Hasler, 'Representational geometry as a fidelity metric for connectome-constrained networks: evidence from the Drosophila visual system', bioRxiv 2026, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.06.10.731214v6 (RSA/CKA on flow/0000; code https://github.com/michaela10c/connectome-fidelity). Beiran & Litwin-Kumar, 'Prediction of neural activity in connectome-constrained recurrent networks', Nature Neuroscience 2025, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-025-02080-4 (bioRxiv 2024.02.22.581667): a connectome alone leaves the dynamics degenerate. Pre-2024 background: Lakshminarayanan et al. 2017 (deep ensembles); Kornblith et al. 2019 (CKA); Frankle et al. 2020 (linear mode connectivity); Wortsman et al. 2022 (model soups); Ainsworth et al. 2023 (Git Re-Basin). Uncertainty on the tracking side: Lee & Waslander, UncertaintyTrack, ICRA 2024, arXiv 2402.12303, code https://github.com/TRAILab/UncertaintyTrack. Project artifacts: runs/flyvis/ensemble_probe.json, runs/flyvis/results/flow/0000/*/validation_loss.h5, runs/fly_reid_controls/report.json, runs/fly_reid_null/compare.json.
relevance: This is mainly a validity problem, not a way to raise HOTA. Every fly re-ID claim rests on one checkpoint (cards fly_signature_reid_v1, fly_matched_controls_v1, fly_connectome_null_v1). Karaneen et al. 2026 show that conclusions drawn from the FlyVis model that is best by task error do not hold up across retraining, so a reviewer will ask for replication across the ensemble. Local checks: validation loss across the 50 models runs from 5.137 (model 000, the best) to 5.678 (model 049), median 5.300; the models are indexed in order of loss (runs/flyvis/results/flow/0000/*/validation_loss.h5). The project probe (runs/flyvis/ensemble_probe.json) loaded all 50 checkpoints and all outputs were finite, but model 049 failed the opposite-horizontal-direction check (49/50 passed). A secondary use: ensemble disagreement could feed a per-track reliability or q_match input at night (N9), and could stabilise the fly's small night increment over its input (+0.010 AP dark vs +0.005 AP bright, runs/fly_reid_controls/strata_bootstrap.json). It does not touch the measured bottleneck, which is the association ceiling at this detector. Pair AP also barely translates into HOTA: +0.25 AP from appearance gave +0.08 HOTA (runs/fly_reid_ablation/report.json).
novelty_overlap: Using and clustering the 50 FlyVis models is Lappalainen et al. 2024. The instability of choosing a model by task error is Karaneen et al. 2026. Representational geometry (RSA/CKA) across the flow/0000 ensemble is Zhou & Hasler 2026. Degeneracy of connectome-constrained solutions is Beiran & Litwin-Kumar 2025. Deep ensembles, CKA-based model comparison and weight averaging are standard ML. Kuklev (arXiv 2609.24565) already uses frozen FlyVis as a descriptor; [uncertain] whether with one model or several was not checked. cannot_claim: ensembles or uncertainty for FlyVis, choosing models by representational geometry, or weight averaging as a contribution. The only project-specific part is the measurement: does the fly's identity signal, and its night increment, hold across ensemble members on BDD100K re-ID pairs? The search found no use of FlyVis ensembles in MOT or re-ID. That absence is not used as a novelty argument (AGENTS.md section 4).
author_results: Lappalainen et al. 2024: 50 models trained on the same connectome and task. Clustering their responses (UMAP + mixture model) gave 4 clusters per cell type, with mean task errors 5.298, 5.317, 5.328 and 5.331. The lowest-error cluster best matched measured T4/T5 tuning. The main accuracy claims rest on median responses of the top 20% of models by validation error. The task is synthetic optic flow (Sintel-based), not real video from a moving camera. Karaneen et al. 2026: they trained two new 50-model ensembles under nominally identical conditions. Cluster mean errors differed by less than 0.08. The lowest-error cluster did not reliably match experimental tuning, post-hoc selection rules were fragile, and correlations between top-ranked models and measured tuning were weaker and more variable. Zhou & Hasler 2026: connectome-constrained networks show stronger direction geometry than random wiring (Spearman r = 0.686 ON, 0.846 ON+OFF, p < 0.0001). Their match to biological T4/T5 tuning is r = 0.930 vs 0.603 for random wiring. They did not test whether geometry predicts task error within the ensemble. UncertaintyTrack (ICRA 2024; BDD100K MOT, 5 Hz annotations, moving camera): using the detector's localization uncertainty in association cut ID switches by about 19% and raised mMOTA by 2-3%. No author reports ensemble effects of FlyVis on re-ID AP or HOTA.
measured_level: Authors: neural-tuning correlations, task error and UMAP clusters (neuroscience level). UncertaintyTrack: IDSw and mMOTA after tracking. Nobody measures FlyVis at pair AP or HOTA. Here the measurement would be pair AP (runs/fly_reid-style pairs), then HOTA/IDF1 after TrackEval, but only if the AP increment is significant.
matched_control: Authors: the original study compared against connectome-free and random variants; Zhou & Hasler use random-wiring baselines. Nobody uses a same-information control (raw input of the same field of view) for the ensemble. In the project these controls already exist for model 000 and must be repeated for each ensemble member. Raw 721-facet input: test AP 0.625 for geometry_hexin vs 0.632 with the fly, +0.006 [+0.0007; +0.0118]. Shuffled fly features: +0.0017 on top of geometry + appearance + input, CI crosses 0. Degree- and sign-preserving connectome null: geometry + fly, intact vs null +0.044 [+0.027; +0.059], better on 29/35 videos; on top of the input +0.003, CI crosses 0 (runs/fly_reid_null/compare.json). For an average of K models, the fair control is K rewired-null models averaged the same way, because averaging by itself reduces noise. The input control is the same for all K models, since they share one retina output.
conditions_breakdown: Authors: no breakdown by illumination or occlusion. Project: existing strata cover it. By luminance, dev+test has 27 dark videos (< 60/255) and 43 bright. By BDD timeofday, it has 29 night, 37 day and 4 dawn/dusk. A per-model night vs day breakdown is the natural test of whether the fly's night increment holds across the ensemble.
cost_here: No new data: all 50 checkpoints are already local (runs/flyvis/results/flow/0000). CPU only, minutes: read the validation losses; compute the response geometry (CKA/RSA) of the 50 models on a fixed stimulus set with flyvis EnsembleView; build a parameter-averaged model within a cluster and check its flyvis validation loss before any video run. GPU: fly signatures must be recomputed for each model, because only the first/last-5-step means of model 000 are cached (runs/fly_signatures stores first_fly/last_fly 34x19, first_hexin 721, etc.). The input, thumbnails, histograms and tracker outputs are identical across models and can be reused. Measured throughput for model 000: about 390 s per 1213-frame video (the 'seconds' field in runs/fly_signatures/*/signatures.json), and 147 videos took about 3.8 h wall time with 7 processes (plan journal, 30.09 18:45). [uncertain] Estimate per extra model: about 1.5-2 h wall time for the 70 dev+test videos with 7 processes, so replicating on 4 models (e.g. 000, 012, 025, 048, spanning the task-error range) is about 6-8 h GPU. [uncertain] Running K models in one pass over the same fovea stream could share the decoding and tracking cost. Evaluation (eval_fly_reid.py ladder + bootstrap) runs on CPU in under 1 h. Long runs only through Start-Process at Idle priority (plan section 9).
expected_effect: Replication: the fly-alone identity signal (+0.10-0.14 AP over geometry) should hold for most members. It is largely carried by the input, which alone gives +0.159 AP over geometry on test; [uncertain] the fly is assumed to be a smooth transform of that input. The increment over the input is small (+0.006 AP on test, +0.010 in the dark) and its sign may vary across members; [uncertain] given Karaneen et al. 2026, some members may show zero. Averaging K signatures: deep-ensemble gains are usually small; [uncertain] a plausible range for the increment over the input is +0.003 to +0.012 AP. The HOTA effect is expected to be 0 within the CI: appearance at +0.25 AP gave only +0.08 HOTA, and stitching with the fly matched stitching without it (test ΔHOTA 0.000; runs/fly_reid_ablation/report.json, plan journal 30.09). Disagreement as a reliability signal: effect unknown; the fly as a reliability head was already redundant to DIS (runs/motion_reliability_lamina). Parameter averaging: may leave the low-loss region because the models are separate optima; [uncertain] averages within a cluster are more likely to keep task error near the cluster mean. Net value: it turns a single-checkpoint claim into an ensemble-level claim, or shows the result is specific to checkpoint 000. That is the main risk the thesis currently carries.
risks: (1) Cost grows linearly with K and a full 50-model run is over budget, so K must be fixed in advance (which models and why), with acceptance criteria written first (AGENTS.md rules 3 and 8). (2) Picking the 'best' member by dev AP after seeing results is exactly the post-hoc selection Karaneen et al. criticise. Select on dev only and report the full distribution across members on test. (3) Ensemble average vs single model differs in two conditions at once (averaging and which model): add a single-model row for each member plus the averaged-null control. (4) Model 049 fails the direction check in the project probe; exclude it or report it separately. (5) Parameter averaging breaks the 'trained FlyVis' semantics and may produce a network that is neither biological nor task-optimal. (6) The frozen detector is not affected. (7) A negative replication must not be presented as novelty (AGENTS.md section 4); it is recorded as completed_negative. (8) Signs seen on short subsets must not be carried over to full runs.
attribution: The ensemble, its training and clustering: Lappalainen et al. 2024 (flyvis). Critique of selecting by task error: Karaneen, Schomburg, Chklovskii 2026. RSA/CKA fidelity on FlyVis: Zhou & Hasler 2026. Deep ensembles, CKA and model soups: Lakshminarayanan 2017, Kornblith 2019, Wortsman 2022. Ours: the fovea-per-track use, the BDD100K re-ID pair protocol, the same-information and connectome-null controls repeated for each ensemble member, and the night/day breakdown.
